gen-gf-noto-serif-ottoman-siyaq-work-san: Work Sans keeps its round bowls clean and its joins the same weight as the strokes, with c tips held well apart. Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq adds a literary, tall-lowercase voice above it.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-archivo: Archivo reads editorial but approachable, its curves opening outward and its x-height standing tall in the line. And Noto Serif Sinhala gives that sans-serif a literary, refined partner with a gentle swing in its strokes.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-fs-asap: Crisp and readable, with a body that nearly matches the capitals. Over a full page, Asap stays easy on the eye while Noto Serif Sinhala supplies a refined, literary note through its tall middle zone.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-fs-epilogue: Approachable and a bit playful, Epilogue bends its wire-thin letters into curvy, unclamped shapes. Noto Serif Sinhala sits above with a faint pull between heavy verticals and lighter horizontals, so a long page keeps a lively, tidy rhythm.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans brings a larger-than-usual x-height and s curves that open wide at both ends, with no thick-thin shift at all. Beside Noto Serif Sinhala, it feels like ink meeting clear glass.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-fs-public-sans: Noto Serif Sinhala has a tall middle zone in every word, with a subtle weight change like etched lines in glass. Public Sans follows with a hefty lowercase and broad counters, so a long passage feels sturdy and trustworthy.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp, laying a thick, heavy-looking strip through the middle of each line with its letters held open. Noto Serif Sinhala earns its keep big and short, where its light stroke modulation can show.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-general-sans: Clean and refined at once, the heading brings a mellow thick-thin difference and the body keeps one width for every stroke. And Noto Serif Sinhala does its best work with that literary swing, while General Sans fills the line smoothly.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-manrope: Noto Serif Sinhala stands out for its tall middle zone, with crossbars a touch thinner than the stems. And Manrope matches it with bright, open curves and a single steady line, making the pair feel approachable.
gen-gf-noto-serif-sinhala-montserrat: Montserrat lets white space lead into every curve, with oversized e and a counters and a line that glides like wire. Noto Serif Sinhala above it could go larger, since its weight change is gradual.
